page: Microsoft Azure F80as_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 80 dedicated physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz without multithreading, paired with 320 GB of memory to yield a consistent 4 GB per core allocation. Hardware acceleration includes instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI, managed beneath the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for persistent data operations.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top decile across central computing metrics. In stress-ng evaluations, the CPU reached 3801.69 in single-core and 288514.33 in multi-core throughput, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 128106.98. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, sustaining 476.73 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 213.43 GB/sec in uncached write tests. Application-level evaluations mirror these raw computation scores, with the instance achieving 203.02 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 110.69 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, alongside top-tier CPU-based LLM prompt processing speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F80as_v7 offers high compute density and strong parallel efficiency by dedicating full physical cores rather than shared or simultaneous multithreading threads. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies entirely on remote storage tiers. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, distributed caching, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks that demand substantial processing power and rapid memory access.
description: Microsoft Azure F80as_v7 is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 80 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 cores running at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 320 GB of RAM. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features a 1:1 physical core-to-vCPU ratio and includes instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AES. It provides no bundled local storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators, depending on remote Azure storage for disk requirements. In benchmark testing, the F80as_v7 consistently registers top-tier scores, delivering 288514.33 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 203.02 million Redis SET operations per second, and 110.69 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Large-block memory reads exceed 476 GB/sec. This configuration offers high raw computation density without hyperthreading overhead, making it well matched for high-concurrency web infrastructure, continuous integration and build workloads, CPU-based machine learning inference, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
